evals.name: infers-before-recommending-conventional-commits
evals.expected_output: Before asking anything, checks the repo's own CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/rules, any commit-msg hook (lefthook.yml, .husky/commit-msg, commitlint config, or a plain Git-managed commit-msg hook resolved via `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` rather than a hardcoded .git/hooks path), and recent git log history for an existing convention. With no signal found, it recommends Conventional Commits (11-type vocabulary: build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test) as the default, marked RECOMMENDED, and does not offer or accept 'security' as a type.
expectations: Checks CLAUDE.md/rules, a commit-msg hook (resolved via git plumbing, not a hardcoded .git/hooks path), and git log history for an existing convention before asking
Recommends Conventional Commits with exactly the 11-type vocabulary when nothing is inferable, marked RECOMMENDED
Does not include 'security' as a Conventional Commits type

evals.name: custom-ticket-prefix-alternative
evals.prompt:
/source-control:setup

This repo uses ticket-prefixed commit messages like WEB-123: fix the thing, not Conventional Commits.
evals.expected_output: Accepts a custom subject_pattern (e.g. ^[A-Z]+-\d+: .+) instead of Conventional Commits, omits the type_list section entirely (no type vocabulary applies to a custom pattern), and writes the custom pattern to .claude/source-control.md.
expectations: Accepts the custom ticket-prefix pattern as subject_pattern instead of forcing Conventional Commits
Omits the type_list section since a custom pattern has no Conventional-Commits type vocabulary
Writes the accepted custom pattern to .claude/source-control.md

evals.name: idempotent-reads-existing-config
evals.expected_output: When .claude/source-control.md already exists, reads it, summarizes the current subject_pattern/type_list/pr_title_pattern/trailer_policy, and proposes changes against that baseline rather than overwriting it blind.
expectations: Detects and reads the existing .claude/source-control.md before proposing changes
Summarizes the current configured values
Does not overwrite the existing config without user confirmation

evals.name: verifies-tracked-not-ignored
evals.prompt:
/source-control:setup

Use the recommended Conventional Commits default.
evals.expected_output: After writing .claude/source-control.md, runs git check-ignore -v .claude/source-control.md to confirm it is not excluded by .gitignore, then runs git status --porcelain -- .claude/source-control.md and reads the worktree column to confirm the content is staged (check-ignore reporting nothing does not by itself prove the file is tracked or staged, and git ls-files --error-unmatch alone would not catch an unstaged rewrite of an already-tracked file). If a .gitignore pattern excludes it, surfaces the matching pattern and offers to fix .gitignore; if the worktree column is non-blank (new or modified-not-staged), stages it with git add, confirms via git diff --quiet that nothing remains unstaged, and prompts the user to commit. Reports success once not-ignored and no-unstaged-changes both hold — it does not require the file to be committed, since a staged-but-uncommitted file legitimately still shows in git status --porcelain output.
expectations: Runs git check-ignore -v .claude/source-control.md after writing the file
Checks staged status via git status --porcelain (worktree column) rather than treating a clean check-ignore result (or index presence alone) as proof the current content is staged
Reports success once the file is confirmed unignored and no unstaged changes remain (e.g. via git diff --quiet), without requiring the file to already be committed
If ignored, surfaces the matching .gitignore pattern and offers a fix rather than silently reporting success
If the worktree column shows untracked or modified-not-staged, stages the file and prompts the user to commit rather than silently reporting success

evals.name: reconfiguration-stages-updated-config
evals.prompt:
/source-control:setup

We're switching from Conventional Commits to a ticket-prefix convention like WEB-123: fix the thing.
evals.expected_output: With an existing, already-committed .claude/source-control.md, rewrites it with the new ticket-prefix subject_pattern, then checks git status --porcelain -- .claude/source-control.md rather than relying on git ls-files --error-unmatch (which would report the path as tracked and appear to pass even though the rewritten content is an unstaged working-tree modification). Because the rewrite produces a modified-but-unstaged file, stages it with git add, confirms via git diff --quiet that nothing remains unstaged, and prompts the user to commit before reporting success.
expectations: Rewrites the existing tracked .claude/source-control.md with the newly accepted convention
Does not rely on index-presence alone (e.g. git ls-files --error-unmatch) to declare the update staged
Detects the unstaged modification via git status --porcelain -- .claude/source-control.md (worktree column non-blank)
Stages the modified file with git add and prompts the user to commit before reporting success, without requiring the commit itself to have happened

evals.name: subject-pattern-always-machine-checkable
evals.prompt:
/source-control:setup

Our convention is: start with a ticket number, then a colon, then a short summary in the imperative mood.
evals.expected_output: Translates the prose description into a single anchored regex (e.g. ^[A-Z]+-\d+: .+) and confirms the translation with the user before persisting, rather than writing the plain-language description itself to subject_pattern. Never persists a free-text subject_pattern.
expectations: Translates a prose-described convention into an anchored regex before persisting
Confirms the translated regex with the user rather than silently guessing
Never writes a plain-language description as subject_pattern in .claude/source-control.md

evals.name: check-renders-effective-merge-with-winning-layer
evals.expected_output: Reports one effective-configuration table across all three layers — a row per key with its resolved value and which layer supplied it — rather than the tracked team file's values alone. The personal overlay's trailer_policy: none wins that key; the team file supplies the rest. Also reports a per-layer presence line, and reports the local overlay's gitignore status as a PASS when it is ignored rather than as the team file's hard-STOP condition.
expectations: Reports the effective merged configuration, not one layer's values presented as the whole convention
Names which layer supplied each resolved key (the overlay wins trailer_policy; the team file supplies subject_pattern)
Treats a gitignored personal overlay as PASS, not as the FAIL a gitignored team file produces
Reports each layer's presence, including absent layers, as INFO rather than failure

evals.name: routes-personal-request-to-local-overlay-not-team-file
evals.prompt:
/source-control:setup apply

I personally want ticket-prefixed subjects like WEB-123: fix the thing on this repo, but don't change what the team uses.
evals.expected_output: Writes .claude/source-control.local.md, not the tracked team .claude/source-control.md, and says which layer it picked before writing. Carries only the keys that differ from the layers below rather than restating the whole config. Verifies the overlay is gitignored — an ignore match is the success condition here, the inverse of the team file's check — never runs git add on it, and if it is not ignored, surfaces the .claude/*.local.* line for the consumer to add rather than editing their .gitignore. Closes by reporting the resulting effective merge, not only the keys written.
expectations: Writes the personal overlay path, leaving the tracked team file unmodified
States which layer it selected before writing
Writes only the differing keys instead of restating every key from the team layer
Treats a git check-ignore match on the overlay as success, and never stages the overlay with git add
When the overlay is not ignored, recommends the .claude/*.local.* gitignore line instead of editing the consumer's .gitignore
Reports the resulting effective merge across layers rather than only the keys just written

evals.name: user-global-write-runs-no-repo-git-checks
evals.expected_output: Writes ~/.claude/source-control.md and runs no git command against it — git check-ignore, git status, and git add all target the repository worktree and would produce a meaningless or confidently wrong verdict on a path outside it (including when the home directory is itself a git repository). Confirms the file exists with the intended content, reports the path, and does not claim the value is staged or committed.
expectations: Writes the user-global path rather than a repo path
Runs no git check-ignore, git status, or git add against the user-global file
Does not report the user-global write as staged or awaiting a commit
Reports the resulting effective merge, noting that an existing team file or personal overlay still overrides these values per key
